title: HAL Hits 52-Week High After Roping In Adani Defence and BEML for Prachand Helicopter
excerpt: India's largest aerospace company partners with Adani Defence Systems and state-owned BEML to produce fuselage structures for 90 Prachand Light Combat Helicopters, sending shares to a record ₹5,149.
body:
• Hindustan Aeronautics Limited has partnered with Adani Defence Systems and BEML to manufacture fuselage structures for 90 Prachand Light Combat Helicopters ordered by the Indian Army, part of a Rs 62,700 crore ($7.2 billion) contract.
  • HAL shares surged to a new 52-week high of Rs 5,149.90 on August 17, extending a 14% rally over the past month as the defence sector sustains its post-Operation Sindoor momentum.
  • The partnership marks a strategic shift toward decentralised manufacturing, with HAL retaining final assembly while outsourcing precision fuselage components to private and public sector partners.
  • First Prachand deliveries are expected to begin in March 2028, with production ramping to 30 units annually across HAL facilities in Bengaluru, Tumkuru, and Nashik.

Partnership Expands Defence Manufacturing Ecosystem

Hindustan Aeronautics Limited has awarded fuselage production contracts to Adani Defence Systems and state-owned BEML for the Prachand Light Combat Helicopter program, bringing two major industrial partners into India's largest-ever helicopter procurement.

The move covers the 90 Prachand helicopters ordered by the Indian Army as part of the Rs 62,700 crore contract signed with the Ministry of Defence in March 2025. A separate tranche of 66 helicopters for the Indian Air Force is also part of the deal.

Under the arrangement, Adani Defence and BEML will manufacture fuselage structures — the core airframe sections that include brackets, ribs, frames, and load-bearing fixtures crafted from aerospace-grade titanium and aluminium alloys. HAL will retain control over final assembly, avionics integration, and flight testing at its facilities in Bengaluru and Tumkuru, with the Nashik complex also being prepared as a Final Assembly and Integration hub.

HAL Shares Touch Record

The partnership announcement pushed HAL shares to a new 52-week high of Rs 5,149.90 on August 17, capping a 14% gain over the past month. The stock has risen nearly 12% over the past year, recovering from a low of Rs 3,479.10 in March 2026.

The rally reflects sustained investor confidence in India's defence sector following Operation Sindoor in May and a string of large Defence Acquisition Council clearances that have totalled over Rs 6.7 lakh crore in procurement proposals during FY26. The Nifty India Defence index has risen sharply from its March lows, with multiple constituents hitting new highs.

BEML, which is contributing to both the Prachand program and winning international orders — including a recent $6.65 million contract from Mauritius for hydraulic excavators — trades near Rs 1,874, within a 52-week range of Rs 1,355 to Rs 2,276.

Why HAL Is Outsourcing

HAL's decision to bring in external partners stems from the sheer scale of the 156-helicopter order. The company's internal manufacturing facilities cannot meet the strict delivery timelines without support, according to defence industry observers.

HAL is leveraging its existing Advanced Light Helicopter Outsourcing (ALH-OS) framework — a proven supply chain and quality assurance system originally built for the Dhruv helicopter program — to onboard partners quickly. This allows suppliers already certified under ALH-OS to begin Prachand component production without a lengthy new qualification process.

"By using the ALH-OS framework, HAL is expanding the Prachand's manufacturing network using a proven and reliable blueprint, avoiding the delays of creating a completely new supply chain."

— Defence News India analysis

The Prachand is a 5.8-tonne twin-engine combat platform designed to operate at altitudes above 5,000 metres in extreme environments like the Siachen Glacier. Powered by Shakti engines developed with France's Safran Group, it is equipped with anti-tank guided missiles, rocket systems, and a 20 mm cannon. India plans to raise indigenous content from 45% to over 65%.

Production Timeline

First deliveries are scheduled for March 2028, with production ramping to 30 units annually. HAL aims to complete all 156 deliveries within five to six years thereafter.

HAL has initiated infrastructure expansion at its Nashik Aircraft Manufacturing Division, including tenders for aluminium partitions and clean-room environments in production shops. Defence analysts note similar upgrades are underway across HAL's facilities to handle advanced avionics, mission computers, and electronic warfare systems.

The programme involves more than 250 domestic companies, predominantly MSMEs, and is expected to generate over 8,500 direct and indirect jobs. A $63 million avionics contract has already been awarded to Bangalore-based Aitech Innovations for display mission computers across the 156-helicopter fleet.

Broader Defence Context

The Prachand partnership adds to a wave of defence sector activity that has powered India's military-industrial complex into a new phase. HAL's order book stands at approximately Rs 2.45 lakh crore, including 97 LCA Tejas aircraft and additional helicopter and transport aircraft orders. Management expects Rs 90,000 crore in order inflows over FY27–28.

For the defence sector more broadly, the government's push toward indigenisation — with domestic procurement now accounting for 75% of total defence spending, up from 54% in FY19 — continues to underpin the structural bull case for Indian defence manufacturers.
